title: Morphogenetic plasticity is not restricted to amphibian or embryonic cells

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Morphogenetic plasticity is not restricted to amphibian or embryonic cells

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The ability of adult, somatic, genetically wild-type human cells to form a novel functional anatomy with new behaviours shows that the plasticity seen in Xenobots is not restricted to amphibian or embryonic cells, and is a fundamental feature of wild-type cells that needs no direct genetic manipulation to unlock.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Introduction

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The ability of adult, somatic, human cells to form a novel functional anatomy, with unique behaviors, reveals that this plasticity is not restricted to amphibian or embryonic cell properties, and is a fundamental feature of wild‐type cells that requires no direct genetic manipulation to unlock.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Gumuskaya G, Srivastava P, Cooper BG, Lesser H, Semegran B, Garnier S, Levin M, “Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells”, Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany) (2024), doi:10.1002/advs.202303575; section “Introduction”. Scope: Genetically wild-type cells generally, generalized from adult human airway epithelium and Xenopus embryonic cells

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-anthrobots-02: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The data refute strict restriction to amphibian embryonic cells, but the broader fundamental-feature generalization greatly exceeds sampled cell types. Existing evidence therefore resolves only the narrow counterexample.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare the frequency and functional diversity of novel self-assembled forms across unedited adult human and amphibian embryonic cells under defined environments.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
One adult human cell type cannot establish a fundamental property of wild-type cells generally.

Novel functional anatomy depends on a contestable baseline.

fields.value:
data existence: 0.62
discriminating power: 0.5
analysis feasibility: 0.72
operationalizability: 0.64
data adequacy: 0.3

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Open Xenobot tracks document novel behavior in frog embryonic cells, which is the baseline this statement says the phenomenon exceeds. The adult human half, and any broader sample of wild-type cell types, is not in a public dataset. A decisive test of the generalization still requires new cell-type runs or release of the Anthrobot cohort.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Apply the same no-edit self-assembly assay to adult somatic human cells and to additional wild-type cell types beyond frog embryonic ectoderm, and score whether a novel motile anatomy appears. One repeated adult-human success would support the narrower contrast with amphibian embryos; failure across further wild-type types would refute the claim that the plasticity is a general feature of wild-type cells.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
What counts as a novel functional anatomy has to be fixed before the universal wording is testable.

Adult human assembly measurements are author-on-request, so the new half of the contrast is not open.

Two epithelial systems cannot separate a general wild-type capacity from a property of ciliated epithelia.

discriminating power: 0.3
analysis feasibility: 0.32
